source.title: Maximum Square Area by Removing Fences From a Field

teaching.hint: What side lengths can be made independently in each orientation after removing intervening fences?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Any pair of horizontal fence coordinates can bound an attainable height; the same holds for vertical widths. A square needs a length in both sets.
solution_outline.approach: Include the fixed borders, enumerate pairwise horizontal distances into a set, and scan pairwise vertical distances for the largest common value. Square that length before taking the modulus.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The horizontal set contains precisely all attainable heights; the running best is the largest attainable width found in that set.
solution_outline.correctness: Every attainable square has one distance from each set, and any shared distance yields a square after removing intervening fences. Maximizing the shared length maximizes true area.
solution_outline.complexity: Expected `O(H²+V²)` time and `O(H²)` space for `H,V ≤ 602` fence coordinates including borders.
solution_outline.pitfall: Comparing areas after modular reduction can choose the wrong square; maximize the actual side first.

source_fidelity_notes: Restates the border coordinates and removability; source diagrams are unnecessary once fence-line coordinates are explicit.
